hpi: The patient is a 67-year-old female who presents with abdominal pain that has been persistent for the last 24 hours. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. The patient reports that the pain is located in the lower abdomen and is associated with nausea and vomiting. On examination, the patient appears to be in moderate distress. Initial laboratory tests reveal elevated white blood cell count and lactate levels. Imaging studies confirm the diagnosis of ischemic colitis. The patient was admitted for further management and surgical consultation was obtained. It is important to recognize the signs and symptoms of ischemic colitis as it can lead to significant morbidity if not treated promptly.
